title: Columbus died convinced he had reached Asia.

beats.text: Columbus died convinced he had reached Asia.
For years, everyone said no. Portugal turned him down. Spain's experts said his numbers were wrong. They were right: he thought the Earth was much smaller.
But once Granada had fallen, Queen Isabella said yes. Columbus demanded the title of admiral, a governorship, and a tenth of the profits. He got them.
On the third of August he sailed west from Palos with three ships and about ninety men.
Weeks of open ocean. The crew came close to mutiny.
Then, on the twelfth of October, a lookout shouted: land! An island in the Bahamas. Columbus named it San Salvador.
He called the people he met Indians, because he was sure he was in the Indies.
He sailed there four times. He died in 1506, still insisting it was Asia.
beats.say: He sailed there four times. He died in fifteen-oh-six, still insisting it was Asia.

beats.text: A year later, a German mapmaker named the new land after another explorer, Amerigo Vespucci. America.
